subject: art-design
title: Final Outcome: Application
welcome_lead: Scale up safely, manage time and bring your idea to life.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE final outcome skills: scaling up, grid method, time management.
final_note: Scaling well preserves the energy of your small studies.

walkthroughs.body_html: Divide your small study into equal squares — say 2 cm. Draw the same number of squares on the large surface — say 10 cm. Copy the contents of each small square into its larger twin. Proportions stay accurate even at four or five times the size.

If your study is square but your final paper is tall and thin, the composition will break. Check the aspect ratio before transferring. Either trim your final surface, or rework the composition for the new shape.

Break the work into stages: surface prep, blocking in, mid-tones, details, finish. Allocate a time to each. Build in a buffer — drying time for paint, breaks to step back. A clear time plan protects the final stages from being rushed.
